interpretations: Rate per status is the mean of per-scan ratios (gbsize ÷ spanmin), skipping scans where either value is missing. Statuses with a rate above the all-status average are kept. The "all-status average" is the simple mean of the per-status rates.
Rate per status is total gbsize ÷ total spanmin (a ratio of sums) over scans with both values present. The "all-status average" is the simple mean of the per-status rates.
Rate per status is the mean of per-scan ratios. The "all-status average" is the mean of per-scan ratios pooled across all matched scans, not the mean of the status rates.
Rate per status is the ratio of sums. The "all-status average" is the pooled ratio of total gbsize ÷ total spanmin across all matched scans.
Scans with spanmin = 0 are excluded to avoid division by zero. Alternatively, they are treated as a missing ratio (NULL).

Scans with a NULL healtheval are treated as their own group (a NULL status). Alternatively, they are dropped. When the NULL status is included, it counts in the all-status average and can be kept or excluded.
Distinct sites per status are counted among all matched scans in that status, including scans with missing gbsize or spanmin. Alternatively, they are counted only among scans with a valid rate.
A status with no valid ratios (rate NULL) is still counted as a status and affects the average count. Alternatively, it is excluded from the all-status average.
"Above" is read as strictly greater than the average. Alternatively, it is read as greater than or equal to.
The final row's average distinct sites is the simple mean of the kept statuses' site counts. Alternatively, it is weighted by scans or by sites.

The "average amount by which their rate exceeds the all-status average" is the mean of (rate − overall average) over the kept statuses. This equals the kept statuses' average rate minus the overall average.
If no statuses are kept, the single row contains NULLs for all three values. Alternatively, no row is returned.
The output is one row with three columns: average rate, average distinct sites, and average excess. Alternatively, the row is presented with the overall average included.

Rate per status is the average gbsize divided by the average spanmin, with each average ignoring its own missing values separately, so the two averages may use different sets of scans. The all-status average is the simple mean of the per-status rates.

Rate per status is the average gbsize divided by the average spanmin, with each average ignoring its own missing values separately. The all-status average is the pooled value of overall average gbsize ÷ overall average spanmin across all matched scans.
queries:
WITH per_status AS (
  SELECT climtune AS status, AVG(gbsize * 1.0 / spanmin) AS rate
  FROM scans
  WHERE gbsize IS NOT NULL AND spanmin IS NOT NULL AND spanmin <> 0
  GROUP BY climtune
)
SELECT status, rate
FROM per_status
WHERE rate > (SELECT AVG(rate) FROM per_status);
SELECT s.healtheval, AVG(sc.gbsize) AS avg_gbsize
FROM scans sc
JOIN sites s ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
GROUP BY s.healtheval;
